# BrutalKit: Full AI and LLM Reference

## 1. Project identity

BrutalKit is a lightweight, dependency-free, CSS-first Neo-Brutalist component library maintained in the repository `ravvdevv/brutal-kit`. It provides reusable primitives for application interfaces without requiring React, Vue, Svelte, or another framework. Frameworks can consume the classes normally.

The library is deliberately small and composable. Do not turn it into a framework, add a runtime dependency for styling, or introduce a global reset.

## 2. Source-of-truth map

| Path | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `src/brutal.css` | Authoritative component CSS and design tokens |
| `src/brutal.js` | Optional browser interactions: tabs and dialogs |
| `dist/brutal.css` | Generated distributable CSS |
| `dist/brutal.min.css` | Generated minified distributable CSS |
| `scripts/build.mjs` | Build pipeline for distributable CSS |
| `tests/` | Automated regression tests |
| `docs.html` | Human-readable documentation site |
| `src/docs.css`, `src/docs.js` | Documentation page styles and behavior |
| `index.html` | Landing page and interactive component demo |
| `src/demo.css`, `src/main.js` | Landing/demo presentation and behavior |
| `AGENTS.md` | Required coding-agent instructions |

Never hand-edit generated `dist/` files as the primary change. Edit `src/brutal.css`, run the build, and commit the generated output alongside the source change.

## 3. Design principles

- Neo-Brutalist visual language: clear geometry, deliberate borders, hard offset shadows, restrained bright accents, and strong typography.
- Prefer legibility and hierarchy over decoration.
- Keep surfaces, spacing, border widths, radii, and shadows consistent through existing tokens.
- Keep the library visually expressive without making every component loud.
- Avoid gratuitous gradients, glassmorphism, neon, excessive rounding, random animation, ornamental dashboards, and decorative UI without a functional purpose.
- Do not introduce arbitrary colors or one-off design tokens when an existing token or semantic modifier is appropriate.
- Respect the consuming application's styles. Do not add broad selectors or reset native elements globally.

## 4. Design tokens

The current defaults in `src/brutal.css` include:

```css
:root {
  --bk-bg: #f7f4ec;
  --bk-surface: #fffefa;
  --bk-ink: #171717;
  --bk-muted: #625f58;
  --bk-yellow: #ffd84d;
  --bk-blue: #a9d9ff;
  --bk-pink: #ffb9c8;
  --bk-success: #c9f2d2;
  --bk-danger: #ffd0cb;
  --bk-border-width: 2px;
  --bk-border: var(--bk-border-width) solid var(--bk-ink);
  --bk-shadow: 5px 5px 0 var(--bk-ink);
  --bk-shadow-sm: 3px 3px 0 var(--bk-ink);
  --bk-radius: 4px;
}
```

Typography and spacing tokens are also defined in the source. Inspect the current source before relying on a token not shown above. Layout utilities support local gap overrides including `--bk-stack-gap`, `--bk-row-gap`, and `--bk-grid-gap`.

Consumers can override custom properties in their own stylesheet. Do not require them to fork the source.

## 5. Component class inventory

Use the exact classes currently implemented in `src/brutal.css` and documented in `README.md` / `docs.html`.

- Buttons: `.bk-button`, `.bk-button--primary`, `.bk-button--secondary`, `.bk-button--blue`, `.bk-button--danger`, `.bk-button--sm`, `.bk-button--lg`, `.bk-button--block`.
- Cards: `.bk-card`, `.bk-card--flat`, `.bk-card__icon`, `.bk-card__title`, `.bk-card__description`.
- Badges: `.bk-badge`, `.bk-badge--blue`, `.bk-badge--success`, `.bk-badge--danger`.
- Forms: `.bk-label`, `.bk-field`, `.bk-field__hint`, `.bk-field__error`, `.bk-input`, `.bk-textarea`, `.bk-select`, `.bk-check`, `.bk-checkbox`, `.bk-switch`.
- Feedback: `.bk-alert`, `.bk-alert--success`, `.bk-alert--warning`, `.bk-alert--danger`.
- Layout: `.bk-stack`, `.bk-row`, `.bk-grid`, `.bk-divider`, `.bk-link`.
- Interactive: `.bk-tabs`, `.bk-tab`, `.bk-tabpanel`, `.bk-accordion`, `.bk-dialog`, `.bk-tooltip`.
- Accessibility: `.bk-visually-hidden`.

Do not invent class names, props, variants, or APIs. Verify the source and documentation before writing examples.

## 6. CSS integration

Use the built stylesheet from jsDelivr:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ravvdevv/brutal-kit@main/dist/brutal.min.css">
```

The default-branch URL is mutable. For production, prefer a published, immutable version tag once the repository has one. Do not claim that an npm package exists: the current package metadata is a private development workspace and no npm package publication is established.

BrutalKit intentionally does not apply a global box-sizing reset or broad element styling. An application may keep its own reset and typography.

## 7. Optional JavaScript integration

The CSS works independently. The optional browser module currently supports tabs and native `dialog` elements.

```js
import { initBrutalKit } from "./src/brutal.js";
initBrutalKit(document.querySelector("#app"));
```

The module automatically initializes `document` when imported in a browser. The initializer uses a WeakSet to avoid duplicate initialization of the same root. If content is inserted later under a separately mounted root, call `initBrutalKit(root)` for that root.

### Tabs contract

- Tablist: `[data-bk-tabs][role="tablist"]`.
- Tabs: `[role="tab"]` with `aria-controls` pointing to their panel.
- Panels: `[role="tabpanel"]` with `aria-labelledby` pointing to the tab.
- Exactly one enabled tab should be selected initially; the initializer chooses a valid enabled tab if markup is incomplete.
- Arrow keys move between enabled tabs and wrap; Home and End move to the first and last enabled tabs.
- Use `aria-orientation="vertical"` for vertical tablists.
- Panels are hidden when inactive.

### Dialog contract

- Use the native `<dialog>` element with `data-bk-dialog`.
- Open triggers use `data-bk-dialog-open="dialog-id"`.
- Close triggers inside the dialog use `data-bk-dialog-close`.
- Provide an accessible name, usually with `aria-labelledby`.
- Native dialog behavior supplies modal focus handling and Escape-to-close; BrutalKit restores focus to the opener after close.
- Always provide a visible close/cancel action.

### Native disclosure and tooltip

Accordions use native `<details>` / `<summary>`. Tooltips use `data-bk-tooltip` as supplementary information. Never put essential content exclusively in a tooltip.

## 8. Accessibility and quality

- Use semantic HTML and native controls where possible.
- Every input needs a programmatic label.
- Icon-only controls need accessible names.
- Preserve visible keyboard focus.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Do not use color as the only carrier of meaning.
- Keep disabled, invalid, hint, and error states distinguishable.
- Maintain usable target sizes and responsive layouts.
- Do not claim WCAG conformance solely because the library has focus styles. Test the composed application.
- When changing interactive behavior, test keyboard operation, focus movement, disabled controls, and nested components.

## 9. Development workflow

Requirements documented by the project: Node.js 22+ and Bun.

```bash
bun install
bun run build
bun run test
bun run dev
```

The package scripts currently map to:
- `build`: `node scripts/build.mjs`
- `test`: `node --test`
- `dev`: `vite --host 0.0.0.0`

Run build and tests after changing library source. Check the generated diff. Add regression tests for behavior changes. Keep documentation examples aligned with the real API.

## 10. AI-assisted programming rules

Before editing:
1. Read `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, and relevant sections of `docs.html`.
2. Inspect the actual source and tests. Do not infer APIs from class names or old examples.
3. Identify whether the change belongs in library source, generated output, demo site, or docs.
4. State the smallest coherent implementation plan when working interactively.

While editing:
1. Preserve the CSS-first, framework-agnostic contract.
2. Avoid new dependencies unless they solve a demonstrated problem; explain the tradeoff.
3. Keep changes focused and modular. Do not rewrite unrelated files.
4. Do not add fake npm commands, fictional package versions, or unverified CDN paths.
5. Do not hand-edit `dist/`; regenerate it through the build script.
6. Keep examples copy-pasteable and accessible.
7. Do not use placeholder controls that look functional but do nothing.

Before finishing:
1. Run `bun run build` and `bun run test`.
2. Review `git diff --check` and the full diff.
3. Verify docs, source, and generated CSS are consistent.
4. Report files changed, commands run, and any tests not run.
5. Do not claim deployment or browser verification unless it was actually performed.
